claims.statement: Coordinates at `#` are expressed in `http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/4326`, with axes bound in the order Latitude, Longitude. Axis order follows that binding and must not be assumed.
claims.negative: Assuming latitude/longitude order, or assuming WGS 84, without reading the binding.

claims.statement: `TimeReceived` is an operational instant (`ingestionTime`), not the time the observed phenomenon occurred, and must not be used as the time axis of the phenomenon.
claims.negative: Using `TimeReceived` as the event time of the observation.

claims.statement: `Timestamp` carries phenomenon time -- when the thing being described happened. Time series, windowing, and joins to other feeds are built on it.
claims.negative: Treating `Timestamp` as the time the record was produced, received, or published, or using a different member for event time.

claims.statement: Successive `Timestamp` values are expected at cadence `irregular`. A cadence is an expectation and not a constraint: a record that departs from it is late, not invalid, and a missing value must not be filled in because the cadence says one was due.
claims.negative: Treating the cadence as a guarantee of completeness or as a validation rule, or interpolating absent values from it.

annotated.note: Strongest is the fix-to-receipt lag residual, a genuinely non-obvious derivation from two differently-roled time members; weakest is the unbracketed `Timestamp` identifier, which is likely to fail to parse in this dialect.

spec.note: Strongest is the disciplined refusal to divide phenomenon-value deltas by ingest-time intervals, which keeps every metric a step rather than a fake rate; weakest is `PERCENTILE_CONT ... OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` mixed with `GROUP BY`, which will not compile as written.

prose.note: Strongest is a clean, bracket-safe single statement whose five metrics are all real derivations spanning continuity, quality, latency and kinematics; weakest is grounding the coordinate reasoning in an assumed WGS-84 earth model rather than the declared binding.

bare.note: Strongest is a plain, well-guarded query that would most likely run as written; weakest is abandoning `Timestamp`, `Latitude` and `Longitude` entirely and spending a metric slot on raw boolean flag shares.
